verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev has a programmatic surface beyond its dashboard: an SDK management API (e.g. `runs.list` with status filters), run handles for checking status, cancelling and retrying, an official MCP server, a CLI for dev and deploy, and scoped per-environment API keys. However, the evidence never claims full UI/API parity. Several actions are documented only in the dashboard: viewing limits, purchasing extra concurrency, managing schedules without redeploying, and configuring runs-list columns. The OpenAPI probe also returned 404 on every candidate path. Missing for 10: documented API parity for dashboard-only actions (schedule CRUD, limits/quota views, concurrency purchase, alert configuration), a published OpenAPI spec, and independent confirmation that the API covers the full UI surface.
